xQueue.title: The Treaty of Sinchula: Bhutan's Himalayan Standoff
xQueue.hook: After seizing two British howitzers in the 1865 Duar War, Bhutan was forced to sign the Treaty of Sinchula, ceding a fifth of its territory to British India.

xQueue.title: Battle Behind the Shrine of Remembrance
xQueue.hook: Over 300,000 people gathered in Melbourne on November 11, 1934, to open the Shrine of Remembrance—a memorial nearly derailed as a tomb of gloom.

xQueue.title: Lion of Khotyn: The Frosty Siege of the Dniester
xQueue.hook: Jan Sobieski forced his enemies to stay awake all night in freezing winds before leading a dawn charge that shattered an army of 35,000 at the Battle of Khotyn.

xQueue.title: The Rise of the People's Liberation Army Air Force
xQueue.hook: The People's Liberation Army Air Force began with just nine cadets in 1924 and a fleet of captured American planes; today it operates the world's second-largest stealth fleet.

xQueue.title: A Tower for the Abolitionist: The Wilberforce Monument
xQueue.hook: The cornerstone for the 110-foot Wilberforce Monument was laid on August 1, 1834—the exact day the Slavery Abolition Act went into effect in the British Empire.

xQueue.title: Defining the Ketch: The Evolution of a Multi-Masted Rig
xQueue.hook: The placement of a single mast forward of the rudder post is the only thing that separates a ketch from a yawl.

xQueue.title: The St. Brice's Day Massacre and the Fate of Æthelred
xQueue.hook: In 1002, King Æthelred II ordered the massacre of all Danes in England, a desperate act of paranoia that failed to stop the Viking conquest of his kingdom.

xQueue.title: Justice in Australia: The Rise of the High Court
xQueue.hook: For decades, Australia's highest court battled for supremacy against British judges in London until the Australia Acts of 1986 finally secured its total independence.
